transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’m having trouble following through on things at work. I’ll start follow-up items after audits or mentoring events with every intention of finishing them, and then a few days later I realize the final email, review note, or form never actually got done. It’s been frustrating, and it’s starting to feel like I need help figuring out why that keeps happening.
Do you find yourself easily getting distracted while working on these tasks?

Yes, very easily. If I’m reviewing an audit file, something like a Slack message, or someone talking outside my office, can completely pull me away from it. Even my own thoughts—like suddenly thinking about marathon training—can derail me, and then I have to work to get back to what I was doing.
Do you find it hard to focus or get distracted in your personal life, outside of work?

Yes, it happens outside work too. I can be doing something at home and a small thing pulls me away—like a notification, a noise, or even just a random thought about my training—and then I’m completely off track. It’s not just at the office.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?

Yes. If I have to sit still for a long review, it starts to feel physically uncomfortable, like pressure building up inside me. I’ll end up standing up, walking to the printer, or finding some reason to move, even if I don’t really need to.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think of myself as acting impulsively a lot, at least not in a way that stands out to me. I’d probably need an example of what you mean.
Do you often interrupt others when they're speaking?

Yes, I do. I catch myself jumping in before someone’s finished, especially with junior auditors. If I think I know the answer or I have an idea, it feels urgent in my head, and I’ll blurt it out before I really stop myself.
Do you have trouble waiting in line or for your turn in other situations?

Yes. Waiting is hard for me. Like if I’m in line at the courthouse records office or sitting in a clinic lobby, I get really tense and impatient. I keep checking my phone, or I’ll go over what I need to say in my head instead of just waiting calmly.
Were you more active or restless than your peers when you were a child?

Yes, I think so, though what I remember more is what teachers wrote about me. Even in elementary school, my report cards would say I was bright, but I lost assignments, rushed through small details, talked out of turn, and needed reminders to finish my work. My mom still jokes that I could ace a test but forget the project sitting in my backpack.
Do you have intense mood swings?
I’m not sure I’d call them intense mood swings. I can get frustrated or overwhelmed, but I don’t usually feel like my mood is suddenly shifting in a big way for no clear reason.
Have you experienced these difficulties with focus, restlessness, and impulsivity for as long as you can remember?

Yes, pretty much. It goes back to elementary school, from what I remember and from what my report cards said. Teachers would say I was bright, but I lost assignments, rushed through details, talked out of turn, and needed reminders to finish my work. My mom still teases me that I could ace a test and then forget the project sitting right in my backpack.
Did you often have difficulty paying attention to details or making careless mistakes in your schoolwork when you were a child?

Yes. I remember that being a problem, and honestly it still is. I can know exactly what I’m supposed to do and still miss a small detail—like a changed date, transposing a number, or leaving some placeholder note in a workpaper. It’s embarrassing, especially in accounting, because details are supposed to be my strength.
Have these difficulties with focus, restlessness, and impulsivity caused you significant problems or stress in your personal or work life?

Yes. It’s caused real problems. At work, the mistakes and the things I don’t follow up on have gotten serious enough that a client review was affected. And now I’m worried people are questioning whether I can really handle the promotion.

At home, it causes stress too. My husband has ended up taking over bills and commitments I agreed to handle, because he can’t really count on me to finish them reliably. It’s frustrating and embarrassing.
Have these difficulties affected your relationships with friends or family in any significant way?

Yes, especially with my husband. He’s had to take over bills and things I had agreed to handle because I don’t always follow through reliably. It makes him frustrated, and I feel embarrassed because it probably seems like he can’t count on me.

With work, too, it affects how people see me. Some mistakes and unfinished follow-up got bad enough to affect a client review, and now I worry people are questioning whether I can handle the promotion.
Have you experienced these same difficulties with focus, restlessness, and impulsivity in both your work and personal life consistently over the years?

Yes. It’s been showing up in both places, but the point where it really started interfering was about a year and ten months ago. That was after I got promoted following a firm-wide award, and suddenly the workload and responsibilities were a lot harder to juggle. Since then it’s been much more consistent and noticeable.
Have you experienced difficulties with focus, restlessness, and impulsivity consistently since childhood, without any significant periods where these issues were not present?

Yes, I think so. Even back in elementary school, my report cards would say I was bright, but that I lost assignments, rushed through details, talked out of turn, and needed reminders to actually finish my work.

My mom still jokes that I could do well on a test but forget the project sitting right in my backpack. So it’s not new, really. It’s just caused bigger problems as an adult.
Do you experience these difficulties with focus, restlessness, and impulsivity in situations where you're doing things you enjoy, like marathon training?

I’m not sure, honestly. I do better when I actually enjoy something, but I haven’t really thought about whether the same issues show up during something like marathon training. I’d have to pay closer attention to that.
Do you find yourself getting easily distracted or having trouble focusing when you're doing something you really enjoy, like marathon training?

Yes, I can. Even with things I care about, my mind can get pulled away pretty easily. Like if I’m reviewing an audit file, a Slack message, someone talking outside my office, or even just a random thought about marathon training can completely knock me off track. Then it takes me a while to get back into what I was doing.
Have these difficulties with focus, restlessness, and impulsivity significantly impacted your daily life activities?

Yes. It’s definitely affecting my day-to-day life now.

At work, the mistakes and things I don’t follow up on have gotten serious enough that a client review was affected. And honestly, I’m worried people are starting to question whether I can really handle the promotion.

At home, it causes problems too. My husband has had to take over bills and commitments I agreed to, because he can’t really count on me to finish them reliably. It’s embarrassing, but that’s where it is.
Do you think your difficulties with focus, restlessness, and impulsivity have caused more problems in your life than they have helped you?

Yes, definitely more problems than help. At work, the mistakes and the things I don’t follow up on have gotten to the point where a client review was affected, and I’m honestly worried people are questioning whether I can handle the promotion.

And at home, my husband has had to take over bills and commitments I said I would handle, because he can’t really count on me to finish them reliably. So… yes, it’s causing real problems.
Have your difficulties with focus, restlessness, and impulsivity caused problems in your friendships or other relationships outside of your marriage?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed it causing major problems with friends, at least not in the same obvious way as work or at home. I guess I’d have to think about that more.
